match_id: MOYES: “I DON’T FEEL LIKE TALKING WELL ABOUT THEM TODAY!”  Everton_Sunderland_2026-05-17_4gSGSGwikbM
team: MOYES: “I DON’T FEEL LIKE TALKING WELL ABOUT THEM TODAY!”  Everton
speaker: Head Coach
quote_text:
David, that was clearly a disappointing afternoon.  Just how do you feel right now? Disappointed,  
what you said. Yeah, disappointed with the outcome  and lots of parts of the game. What frustrated you  
most? Well, obviously the result frustrated  me most because I didn't think it was quite  
that. I didn't think that it was a true reflection  really on the game, but that's what it ended up.  
What were you saying to the players at half-time?  Obviously, you got in at the break, got the goal  
just before then, had a little bit of momentum.  What was your message to the players? Keep doing  
what we were doing. We hadn't started the game  awfully well. They kept the ball quite well, but I  
thought we looked a bit of a threat. We'd sort of  grown into the game. We get a goal not long before  
half-time. They started the second half much  better. They had got themselves a few free kicks,  
three or four free kicks in the first four or  five minutes, which didn't help, and we gave away  
a terrible first goal. I thought once it went one  each, I thought we were probably the better team  
leading in that period of the game. I thought  the game sort of swayed at different times and  
unfortunately we gave away a second goal, which  meant that we were half chasing the game after  
that. Quite early in the second half, it looked  like Jake O'Brien might have picked up an injury.  
The first half for me. He got it in the first  half from a challenge that he had. He went down  
just before half-time, so we knew he had taken  quite a big knock. Just after that, you could  
see Patterson went to warm up and it looked like  you were thinking about bringing Coleman on. What  
was the thought process with keeping on with him?  Because we thought he was injured when he went off  
the pitch at the bottom and then we got told that  he was able to get through it at that period. They  
were having a series of three or four corner kicks  at the moment, which I needed big Jake's height.  
Thank you. Next. Iliman's had two opportunities in  each of the last two games at home here at crucial  
times and not taken either. Does that just sort of  show what he needs to develop in his game? Yeah,  
I think that those players have been so good  for us in the early part of the season. I  
think the second half of the season has  looked as if we've just run out of goals,  
mainly from the likes of Iliman, Kiernan a little  bit as well. So I think Iliman especially has had  
big opportunities in a few of the games, which  in the past we've seen him score. He scored a  
great goal against Chelsea here, but since then  we've had quite a lot of opportunities in the  
games and we've not been able to take them  to win the games which we've needed because,  
as we know, we've not been overly generous with  our centre-forwards' goals. So it's been sort of  
Kiernan and Iliman who've been required to step  up for us mainly and it has sort of just dried up  
in the last month or so. Andy, did you have your  hand up? David, it's been a disappointing end to  
the season for you now. What do you think you need  over the summer to build on the positives earlier  
in the campaign? I think we need to go again  and try and restart another part. Let's be fair,  
we're trying to build something which  is going to be good as time goes on.  
We put ourselves in a decent position most of the  season to talk well about the team, but I don't  
feel like talking well about them today because  it was a big moment for us and we weren't able  
to take it. So we need to try and find a way of  improving that, and that mainly always means that  
we're going to have to bring in other players and  try and see if we can step up again. Barry. Hi,  
David. It was another game where Everton had  the lead and couldn't quite see it through,  
so wondering from your perspective, what do you  think has changed from the start of the season,  
that the side was holding those leads at the start  but has not been able to do it in recent weeks? I  
don't think there's any one reason for it. I think  that today's was a pure mistake. I think the other  
games, and let's be fair, we're just off the back  of two or three of the worst decisions for us,  
which have made our results look far worse than  they are. We've actually, in truth, played pretty  
well. Maybe not so much today, but in the other  games we've played pretty well. We've lost out in  
a couple of penalty kick decisions which have cost  us points. So any one of those other games, if the  
points had gone in our favour, we would be  saying we'd be disappointed a bit today, but  
we would still be thinking that we've done okay.  So I do think that, yeah, it's not really like  
us. We've lost three here against Man City and we  lost three here today, and especially when we're  
playing Sunderland, who are not a side who score  many goals in truth, so it should have been  
something which we should be better at. But as I  said, I think the third one got away from us and  
that's why I said a bit about not being sure the  result was quite right. The third got away when  
we were having to try and find a way of getting a  goal back. Okay, folks. Okay, cheers. Thank you.
title: MOYES: “I DON’T FEEL LIKE TALKING WELL ABOUT THEM TODAY!”  Everton 1-3 Sunderland
